items.caption: 🔌 Connection: The instance runs below an MQTT server/client (splitter) and receives everything HeishaMon publishes. The only mandatory setting is the MQTT base topic - it must match the base topic configured in HeishaMon's own web interface exactly (default of both sides: panasonic_heat_pump). Everything else in this form is optional.
"Debug: unknown topics" writes topics this module does not know yet to the instance debug window - only useful when investigating new firmware topics, leave it off otherwise.

📋 Datapoints: Variables are created automatically as soon as HeishaMon publishes the corresponding topic - the Received column shows what your unit actually sends. Deactivating a datapoint hides its variable (object ID and archive data remain; reactivating simply shows it again); datapoints whose variable does not exist yet are not created while deactivated. Reorder rows by drag & drop - variable positions and links follow the order. "Update variable names" renames only variables that still carry an old default name (your own names stay untouched); "Reset order and selection" restores the default order in the open form - nothing is saved until you click Apply.

🌡️ 1-Wire sensors: Additional temperature sensors (e.g. DS18B20) on the HeishaMon 1-Wire bus are detected automatically at their first reading and appear in their own list for naming and activation - no manual MQTT setup needed.

🔗 Link structure: Creates a grouped category tree (Operation, Heating, DHW, ...) with links to all active datapoints - useful for a tidy WebFront navigation instead of one long flat list. Requires a target category; links of deactivated datapoints are removed automatically.

⚡ External energy meter: If a meter (e.g. Shelly 3EM or an S0 meter wired directly to the HeishaMon board) measures the heat pump supply line, select its power and energy counter (kWh, cumulative) variables, and set the power unit (W or kW) to match. The module then reports the measured electrical power instead of the unit's rough estimate and calculates the measured COP plus the daily performance factor. The minimum power threshold prevents misleading COP values from standby noise. Without an external meter the module uses the unit's own power values; heat pumps of the K/L series and newer report invalid values in the standard power topics, so the module automatically uses the precise values of the extra data block (extra/ topics) as soon as they arrive. If MeterHub already has a meter assigned to function "heat pump", it is used automatically - no click needed, and the module keeps following later changes to that assignment. A status line shows what is actually in effect; your own meter (optional panel below the fields) always takes priority over MeterHub.

🌡️ Heating automation: Optionally switches only the room heating on and off (and, with a dew point source, cooling) from the outside temperature means and your room temperatures. Hot water is never affected. Turn it on with the switch variable "Heating automation"; switching it off restores the heating. Humidity and room sensors are found automatically (your own selection overrides).

💡 Energy saving check: Assesses the settings received from the unit (DHW target, reheat delta, backup heater enables, heating-off threshold, heating curve, pump duty) and the real cycling behavior (runtime per compressor start) against reference values from the documented HeishaMon example rulesets and the Panasonic service manual. Display only - nothing is changed automatically.

⚙️ Energy saving rulesets: Deploys a parameterized short-cycle guard to the HeishaMon board itself, where it keeps running even if WiFi or IP-Symcon fail. Covers heating by default; "Also protect cooling mode" adds an independent, identical guard on the cool request, since the heat request has no effect while cooling. Deploying replaces the entire ruleset stored on the board; the firmware validates every upload and keeps the previous ruleset on errors.

🔄 Reboot watchdog: If the heat pump stays offline via MQTT for longer than configured, the module triggers a restart of the HeishaMon board via its /reboot endpoint (at most once every 30 minutes). Helps when MQTT hangs but the board's web server still responds; if the board is entirely off the network, its firmware keeps reconnecting on its own.

📊 Archiving: Automatically enables logging for the monitoring datapoints (electrical and thermal power, flow/return/outside temperature, COP, defrost, compressor starts/hours, WiFi quality, MQTT reconnects) so time-series tiles can show day/week/month/year charts. Each variable is activated only once - disabling logging manually in the archive handler is respected permanently.

🆕 Extra commands: Optional switchable variables for the two relays of the large HeishaMon board and the SmartGrid mode (digital replacement for the native SG ready dry contacts; requires the heat pump service setting "Optional PCB" = Yes). Write-only - the displayed value reflects the last command sent, not a confirmation from the unit.

🩺 Board diagnostics: The variable group "Board diagnostics" (WiFi quality, uptime, MQTT reconnects, bus read quality, active rules, firmware version) is fed from the HeishaMon stats topic. When connections drop, its archived history shows the cause: weak WiFi, MQTT hangs, hidden restarts (uptime jumps) or cable/CRC issues.

🤝 Integration: Other NRG-Stack modules (energy management, system schematic, heat pump monitor) find this heat pump automatically via HEISHA_GetFunctions - no manual variable assignment needed. Scripting commands (including reading and setting heating curves and operating functions) and the version history are documented in the README and CHANGELOG of the module; questions and feedback are welcome in the module thread (link in the forum hint below).

Which variable fits as the power source?

popup.caption: Which variable fits as the power source?

items.caption: Select a variable with the CURRENT power draw, measured on the heat pump supply line only (e.g. the heat pump phase of a Shelly 3EM, or the datapoint "S0 meter 1: power" if an S0 meter is wired to the HeishaMon board). Why must the counter be cumulative?

popup.caption: Why must the counter be cumulative?

items.caption: Select a CUMULATIVE kWh counter (total energy, ever increasing - e.g. the Shelly total counter or the datapoint "S0 meter 1: energy total"). Do NOT select a today/daily value that resets at midnight - the daily performance factor is calculated by this module itself from the counter. The unit must be kWh. Leave empty to use MeterHub automatically instead, if installed.

items.caption: Minimum power for COP calculation
Why a minimum power threshold?
Below this power, COP (measured) reports 0 instead of a misleading ratio - protects against standby noise (typically a few watts).

Switches ONLY the room heating on and off - never the whole heat pump. The hot water keeps running in every state. The decision is based on the outside temperature (a short and a long mean, 24 h and 48 h by default, with hysteresis and a lock time) and optionally on your room temperatures. Frost protection always wins. Turn the switch variable "Heating automation" on to let it act; until then it only observes.

items.name: HeatAutoStatus
items.caption: HEATAUTOSTATUS

items.name: HeatAutoEnabled
items.caption: Use heating automation
How does the heating automation decide?

popup.caption: How does the heating automation decide?

items.caption: Every 15 minutes the module checks, in this order: (1) Frost protection: outside mean below the frost threshold, or any room below 10 °C, always means heating on - lock time ignored. (2) Outside mean below "heating on" threshold: heating on. (3) Both outside means above "heating off" threshold: heating off. The long mean makes switching off slow on purpose, one warm day does not shut the heating off. (4) In between: your rooms decide, if selected - too cold for the delay time: heating on; warm enough for the delay time: heating off; otherwise the state is kept (hysteresis). (5) After every change the new state is kept for the lock time (switching on again after only a quarter of it). Missing outside data means heating stays on. After each command the module reads the operating mode back and retries up to three times; the unit never acknowledges commands itself. If the operating mode is changed from outside (e.g. in the dashboard), the automation accepts that and waits for the lock time before acting again - only frost protection acts immediately. When you switch the automation off, a disabled heating is turned on again.

🏠 Room temperatures (optional)

Rooms refine the decision between the two thresholds. Without your own selection the module uses one temperature sensor per room of the Raumstruktur module, if installed (at least three rooms, outdoor and unheated rooms excluded, median of the rooms). Select your own sensors to override: wall sensors of the rooms you want to keep comfortable, not radiator thermostats right at the heater, smoke detectors or sensors that sometimes report 0. Your own selection uses the mean.

❄️ Cooling (optional, only in summer operation)

Cooling uses the operating mode "Cooling + hot water". It is only allowed when the dew point is known and the lowest cooling target of the heating curve stays above the dew point plus the safety margin - otherwise water would condense on radiators and pipes. The module finds humidity sensors of the rooms on its own (outdoor and soil moisture excluded) and uses the highest value; you can name your own humidity variables or a dew point variable instead.

items.name: HeatAutoCooling
items.caption: Cooling by the automation
Why is a dew point source required?

popup.caption: Why is a dew point source required?

items.caption: Cooled radiators and pipes below the dew point of the room air collect condensation water. The module therefore only starts cooling if a dew point (or humidity) source is selected and the lowest cooling target of your heating curve is at least the safety margin above the dew point. While cooling, it stops immediately as soon as the measured flow temperature falls below dew point plus margin. Without a source cooling stays off. Check the cooling curve of the heat pump yourself as well - the module does not change it.

items.caption: The address under which the HeishaMon web interface is reachable in your network (e.g. 192.168.2.16) - you can find it in your router's device list or via the hostname configured in HeishaMon. items.caption: Only above outside temperature
How does the short-cycle guard work?

popup.caption: How does the short-cycle guard work?

items.caption: After each compressor stop, the heat request is lowered for the configured time so the compressor does not restart immediately - fewer starts mean better efficiency and longer compressor life. Below the outside temperature threshold the suppression ends immediately (cold weather takes priority). Template: Compressor-Short-Cycle-Guard from the HeishaMon repository.

items.name: GuardCoolingEnabled
items.caption: 🆕 Also protect cooling mode

items.name: GuardMaxOutsideTempCool
items.caption: Only below outside temperature
Why does cooling need its own guard?

popup.caption: Why does cooling need its own guard?

items.caption: The heat request suppression above has no effect while the unit is cooling - cooling demand is a separate value the heat pump does not touch during heating. This adds an independent, identical suppression on the cool request, so short-cycling is also avoided in cooling mode. Above the outside temperature threshold the suppression ends immediately (hot weather takes priority - mirrors the cold-weather override for heating).

items.caption: If the heat pump stays offline via MQTT for longer than the configured time, the module triggers a restart of the HeishaMon board via its /reboot endpoint (uses the IP address entered above). This helps in the most common hang (MQTT dead, web server still responding); if the board has dropped off the network entirely, its firmware keeps reconnecting on its own and only a power cycle helps. At most one restart attempt every 30 minutes.
